source.section: PIT-ADJ instructions PDF page 7, line 25, Table 2 and Examples 1 and 2; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12; Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 60,000.00 + taxable Social Security (85% of gross 40,000.00) 34,000.00 = 94,000.00. Federal taxable income = 94,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 additional for age 65 or older = 76,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, single. Line 9 federal AGI 94,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 17,750.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 94,000.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 36,667.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 13 age 65 or older: Table 1 (single) row for federal AGI 94,000.00 gives 0.00 x 1 qualifying = 0.00; line 25 Social Security: federal AGI 94,000.00 does not exceed the Table 2 maximum 100,000.00 (single), so the 34,000.00 included in AGI is exempt = 34,000.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 34,000.00. Line 17 = 94,000.00 + 0.00 - 17,750.00 - 0.00 - 34,000.00 = 42,250.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 76,250.00 - 34,000.00 = 42,250.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 42,250.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 5,500.00 = 82.5 + 3.2% x 11,000.00 = 352 + 4.3% x 17,000.00 = 731 + 4.7% x 8,750.00 = 411.25; total 1,576.75, to the cent 1,576.75. The table row over 42,200 to 42,300 gives 1,577; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 1,576.75.
